args.message: Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was importing and applying `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring (and FIN-212) specify banker's rounding. This made the nightly build fail because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects `Decimal("2.665")` to round to `Decimal("2.66")`.

## Changes
- Replaced the `ROUND_HALF_UP` import with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` and used it in `quantize`.

## Testing
- CI run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` passed, including `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even`.
args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

trace.final:
Done. Here's what happened:

**Root cause:** `src/money.py` imported and used `ROUND_HALF_UP` while its docstring (and FIN-212) specify banker's rounding. As a result, `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` failed — e.g. `2.665` rounded to `2.67` instead of `2.66`.

**Fix:** Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and committed a one-line correction so `round_money` now imports and applies `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in its `quantize` call.

**CI:** Triggered run `ci-0001` on commit `08d3cd5986` — it passed.

**PR:** Opened PR #101 ("Fix round_money to use banker's rounding per FIN-212") against `main`, with alex requested as reviewer. It has not been merged, since merging requires code-owner approval. PR link: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101
